messages.subject: Re: On input Subspecies
messages.body_plain:
Hi Gengping,

Thanks for using Wallace and give us your thoughts. Unfortunately, there is no way to handle a subspecies name inside of Wallace. This is because the internal code works with a binominal name. My suggestion is that you create a CVS file for each subspecies. You can download your table from Wallace using a species name for the component 1. Then, use the spreadsheet software of your preference to create files per subspecies. And then, open Wallace again to upload your localities in the user-specified occurrence data.

Future versions of Wallace will support to run several species at the same time. Supporting subspecies name could be useful for the next release. I will discuss this enhancement with the dev-team.

Best,
Gonzalo

messages.subject: Re: On Process Occs module
messages.body_plain:
Hi Gengping,

I don't see the point to use the removed points for testing your model. These removed localities have a spatial correlation with your remained localities. If you are using these localities for testing your models, you can bias your evaluation metrics.

If you still want to get these points, I suggest you to use the 'spthin' package on R. The removed localities cannot be retrieved on Wallace.

Best,
Gonzalo

messages.subject: Re: On Process Occs module
messages.body_plain:
Hi- agreed that using the points that have been removed due to spatial thinning defeats the purpose of spatial thinning. I recommend following up on spatial thinning by using spdep or another R package to run Moran's I a few times just to see if various levels of spatial thinning have even had the desired effect, which is to reduce false positive predictions by reducing spatial autocorrelation. There are also situations where spatial thinning may not be the best idea, even if it does reduce spatial autocorrelation, depending on the purpose of the model and the peculiarities of the species and study site. I'm working on a very small spatial scale currently (50X20 km) and boosted regression trees and generalized linear models are producing fairly strong cross validated and ground-truthed models at a distance of only 100 meters between presence/pseudoabsence points, but this is in a very heterogeneous habitat. On the contrary, using the same data and the same site, WorldClim variables work best when the presence/pseudoabsence are heavily thinned to a 1 km distance.

A multimodeling approach using several different calibrations and tests is in my opinion the best way to generate models that are useful and fit for purpose.

I guess this is kind of verbose, sorry,

Peter Breslin
Arizona State University

messages.subject_clean: Report and looking for help on some issues
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
First, my deepest congrats for this fine piece of software. I can see it has an enormous potential...but...I would like to report some issues I am experiencing preventing even to carry out my first analysis.

Environment: Mac OSX Mojave (16 Gb RAM), clean installation of latest versions (January 22th) of R, RStudio and Java (did check that all are 64 bits). PATh variables correctly assigned for the jdk. I did the clean installation after the issues reported below. Maxent.jar (v 3.3.3) in the directory of "dismo"

- occurrences: a list of 600 points: loaded and displayed correctly, thinned by 2 km (total: 482 occurrences)
- environmental variables: 6 TIFF layers from MODIS: loaded correctly (size, about 2.8 Mb each). By the way, the issues also happen if using WorldClim.
- background: a polygon made by myself with the coordinates of the 4 corners: correctly displayed
- 10,000 background points
- Jacknife (k=n)
- maxnet method: only "L", regularization and multiplier step value by default, without clamping.

Problem 1: after "run" the model, RStudio states

There are 129 background records with NA for at least one predictor variable.
                  Removing these records from analysis, resulting in 9871 records...
(OK to here)

and then later

15776 grid cells found with at least one NA value: these cells were excluded from raster predictions.
Warning: Error in [: (subscript) logical subscript very long
  95: regfun
  94: maxnet::maxnet
  93: modelTune.maxnet
  92: tuning
  91: ENMeval::ENMevaluate
  90: <reactive> [modules/mod_c6_maxent.R#94]
  74: mod.maxent
  73: observeEventHandler [/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.5/Resources/library/wallace/shiny/server.R#519]
   2: shiny::runApp
   1: run_wallace

And then the web browser "hangs" and I must to restart again. Tested in both Safari and Firefox. Tests also in Windows 7. No way.

Problem 2: If I use the maxent.jar option, then rJava does not load (it is not installed as a dependency of wallace. I installed "manually" from CRAN) and the error message is:

Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘rJava’:
 .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'rJava', details:
  call: dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...)
  error: unable to load shared object '/Users/aestrada/Library/R/3.5/library/rJava/libs/rJava.so':
  dlopen(/Users/aestrada/Library/R/3.5/library/rJava/libs/rJava.so, 6): Library not loaded: /Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk-11.0.1.jdk/Contents/Home/lib/server/libjvm.dylib
  Referenced from: /Users/aestrada/Library/R/3.5/library/rJava/libs/rJava.so
  Reason: image not found

By the way, both rJava.so and libjvm.dylib are in the right directory. I followed every instruction in Github to make this library to work, without success (you know redirecting the PATH, etc.)

Will acknowledge every help. I begun to enter into "desperate mode" :-) [you know some 500 models to develop and project...]

Thanks everyone,
Agustín

messages.body_plain:
Hi Agustín,

Thanks for writing to us about these issues. Although you have a lot of info (thanks again), I need more to figure out what is happening.

Problem 1:
I would like to know if you can share us your points and csv-polygon to tried to reproduce your error. If the worldclim variables that you mention are user-specified (no downloaded on Wallace), I also would like to obtain some of your rasters. I think that a GIF or a video screen recording of all your workflow on Wallace is very helpful to discard any user-input problem.

https://www.any-video-converter.com/mac-tutorial/record-videos-on-mac.php

Problem 2:
The first problem loading rJava is because I didn't specify it as a suggested package on the last version (our problem). 'rJava' was a dependency on the previous version of ENMeval, so it was always loaded on Wallace before. We will fix this issue in the next version.

But this problem should be fixed easily by installing 'rJava' manually (you did it) and be sure that it is correctly loaded on R. Are you having the same problem on Windows machines? Did you get the same error when you try to load just 'rJava' on the console?

Maybe this link is helpful:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/30738974/rjava-load-error-in-rstudio-r-after-upgrading-to-osx-yosemite

Best,
Gonzalo
